direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.question: Do I need planning permission?
direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.answer: Usually not, since 27 July 2026. External wall insulation to a house is exempted development (Class 63, S.I. No. 341 of 2026) if it's no more than 150 mm thick on the front, rear or gable, doesn't encroach on a public road, and doesn't materially change how the house looks against its neighbours. direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.question: How long does it take?
direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.answer: Weeks rather than days, with scaffold up: most houses take 2 to 3 weeks, weather permitting, and NSAI says an average semi-D should be done within a fortnight. See how long it takes .

direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.question: Can I stay in the house during the work?
direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.answer: Usually yes. The work is outside, though there's scaffold, noise and some disruption.

direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.question: Will my windows look sunk in?
direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.answer: The wall gets thicker, so the windows sit deeper. New, longer sills and neat reveals keep it tidy.

direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.question: Do I need an ESB Networks service alteration?
direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.answer: Maybe. SEAI says you may need one for external wall insulation, depending on how the cable reaches the house. Check with your contractor and ESB Networks before work starts.

direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.question: Does the wrap change my BER?
direct_answer_faqs_for_seeding.answer: It usually improves it, because the walls lose less heat. A post-works BER is part of the grant process.
